what: How rail fares map onto GTFS
title: Heavy Rail CIF to GTFS - Train Timetables
text: Rail fares set per flow: origin/destination pair, fare route (“via permitted”, “via London”, …) ticket type. flow endpoint always single station - can station cluster (stations share fares) group station “LONDON TERMINALS”. maps onto two GTFS fare models follows: tickets converted controlled arguments: fares_ticket_class (standard/first), fares_ticket_type (single/return/season) explicit fares_ticket_codes; fares_rider_categories fares_railcards choose passenger types (v2 ). default walk-tickets - Anytime, -Peak Super -Peak families - converted (fares_walkup_only = TRUE); feed also prices trade, carnet advance-purchase tier tickets, misleadingly cheap journey planner. See ?gtfs_add_railfares details.

what: Scenario conversion: a specific travel date, time and booking date
title: Heavy Rail CIF to GTFS - Train Timetables
text: GTFS carry full restriction model rail ticketing (validity varies date, time, route train). converter can evaluate restrictions conversion time, one concrete scenario, output plain GTFS containing exactly fares available scenario: Three things happen: records read valid travel date (feed contains current future fares rounds); restriction data (RST file) evaluated date departure time: -Peak Super -Peak fares dropped time restriction makes invalid (e.g. departing 09:30 weekday), fares date-banned travel date; booking date, Advance tickets whose booking horizon (TAP file) satisfied added tier prices, instead excluded. recommended way fare-sensitive analysis (e.g. comparing peak vs -peak accessibility, walk-vs advance pricing): build one feed per scenario compare. Omit fares_travel_time apply date-level restrictions; omit fares_booking_date walk-fares . Two caveats. Advance availability quota-controlled per train reservation system public feed, Advance prices bookable tiers - best case. restriction evaluation covers date bands departure-time bands (network-wide origin-station-specific); arrival-based, via-based train-specific restrictions, easements minimum-fare windows treated “fare remains valid”, filter errs towards keeping fare.
code: # Fares for a journey departing 08:00 on Monday 3 August, # with the ticket bought on 1 July gtfs <- atoc2gtfs("myfolder/timetable.zip", ncores = 3,                   fares = "myfolder/fares.zip",                   fares_version = 2,                   fares_travel_date = as.Date("2026-08-03"),                   fares_travel_time = "08:00",                   fares_booking_date = as.Date("2026-07-01"))

text: Like bus fares conversion (see Adding Fares - NeTEx GTFS vignette), converting rail fares GTFS lossy. Choices surfaced arguments; losses buy back listed . GTFS v1 express ticket choice passenger types. fares_version = 1 every station pair gets exactly one price: cheapest fare among ticket types selected (default: standard-class singles). Child, railcard return fares ignored. Use v2 need . Ticket time restrictions carried output. -Peak Single emitted price, GTFS say invalid 08:00, journey planner sees Anytime -Peak product stations choose correctly. Either convert scenario (fares_travel_date/fares_travel_time ), restrict conversion Anytime products (e.g. fares_ticket_codes = c("SDS", "SOS")). Returns priced round trip. GTFS native return ticket; return product’s amount price whole return journey attached single leg. Season tickets excluded default reason (feed price weekly rate). Advance fares appear booking scenarios. Advance tickets quota-controlled: flow file lists price tiers information tier sale train. default dropped (fares_walkup_only = TRUE); fares_booking_date scenario bookable tiers included best-case prices. Child railcard prices calculated, quoted. feed derives adult fare via status discount file (typically 50% children). UK2GTFS applies percentage flat-fare/minimum-fare caps, industry rounding rules railcard minimum-fare rules, calculated price can differ retail price pence. flows placed. Flow endpoints stations (county codes, travelcard zones without member stations) stations absent timetable dropped, message reporting count. TOC-specific ticketing simplified. Fares attached one national “rail” network (v2) route (v1), .e. treated inter-available. Operator-tickets (TSP file) cross-London rules modelled. Feed size. national flow file holds ~700,000 flows ~7 million prices. national v1 conversion expands clusters station pairs produces multi-million-row fare_rules.txt; v2 stays close source size clusters become areas. written fine gtfs_write(), consumers vary accept.

title: Adding Fares - NeTEx to GTFS (v1 and v2)
text: Timetables fares published separately UK: Timetables come TransXChange XML converted GTFS [transxchange2gtfs()]. gives stops, routes, trips, stop_times calendars, fares. Fares come NeTEx XML (DfT “fxc” fares profile) separate BODS fares archive. NeTEx large, general European standard; UK profile uses slice , slice still far richer anything GTFS can express. job functions read NeTEx fares, line GTFS routes already built, write fares either GTFS fares specification: GTFS “v1” - original fare_attributes.txt + fare_rules.txt (plus zone_id stop). GTFS-Fares-v2 - newer, richer areas, fare_products, fare_leg_rules, rider_categories, fare_media networks tables. two genuinely different data models, supported choose fares_version.

what: The NeTEx fare model (what one file contains)
title: Adding Fares - NeTEx to GTFS (v1 and v2)
text: BODS fares archive, one XML file describes fares one line, one direction, one product - example “Beestons line 91, Inbound, Adult Single”. single registered service therefore spreads across many files (adult/child x single/return x inbound/outbound). fares usually zone--zone fare triangle: line’s stops grouped handful fare zones (FareZone -> list ScheduledStopPointRef); every origin-zone / destination-zone pair points price band (DistanceMatrixElement -> PriceGroupRef); price band monetary amount (PriceGroup -> Amount). meaning “travelling zone zone B line costs GBP X passenger type”. smaller number files instead describe single flat fare (one price whole line, zones); read single zone-less fare.

what: Matching fares to routes, and a national report
title: Adding Fares - NeTEx to GTFS (v1 and v2)
